description.narrative:
BridgeTheGap is a 12-month cooperation between Vijana Economic Front and Copenhagen Youth Network to address the youth “Decent WorkDeficit” through joint policy and advocacy. The project runs in Nairobi’s informal settlements and Copenhagen’s local youth employment contexts, engaging marginalised young people (including low-income youth, and graduates facing structural exclusion from labour market entry). Youth Citizen Researchers will gather lived-experience evidence on barriers to decent work, which will feed into parallel advocacy bootcamps and cross-continental Policy Labs. By May 2027, the partners will co-produce the Nairobi–Copenhagen Youth Labour Manifesto and formally present policy recommendations to the Kenyan Ministry of Labour and the Danish Ministry of Employment through youth-led dialogue forums. The project strengthens long-term cooperation by establishing a cross-continental youth advocacy network and open learning resources that remain usable beyond the grant.
Our goal is to developa Youth-Led Decent Work Framework thatstrengthens youth influence on labour policy in both Kenya and Denmark.
Short-term (12 months): We will train 250 young people (150 in Nairobi and 100 in Copenhagen) in evidence-based advocacy, labour rights awareness, and digital soft skills. Youth Citizen Researchers will generate lived-experience evidence that will feed into the co-production of the Nairobi–Copenhagen Youth Labour Manifesto. This joint policy document will be formally presented to the Kenyan Ministry of Labour and the Danish Ministry of Employment through dedicated dialogue forums
Long-term: We expect a shift in how youth-led SMEs are regulated in Kenya (e.g., lower formalizationbarriers) and improved "early activation" pathways for graduates in Denmark. The ultimate impact is the creation of a permanent cross-continental network that holds power to account, ensuring Sustainable Development Goal 8 (Decent Work) is met through youth-centered legislation rather than just corporate-led growth.

participating-org.narrative:
Copenhagen Youth Network (CYN) is a non-governmental, non-profit organisation established in 2012 and based in Copenhagen’s North-West district, one of the city’s most diverse and densely populated areas. CYN works closely with marginalized and underserved young people at local, regional, national, and international levels.
Vision: CYN envisions inclusive, democratic societies where young people are empowered to participate actively and confidently in civic, social, and economic life at local, European, and global levels.
Mission: CYN’s mission is to promote social inclusion, active citizenship, and mental well-being through intercultural exchange, non-formal education, and community-based recreational activities. We create safe and engaging spaces where young people from diverse ethnic and socio-economic backgrounds can build skills, self-respect, and a sense of belonging.
Objectives: CYN aims to: - Strengthen social inclusion and democratic participation among young people with fewer opportunities, including NEETs, refugees, and migrants - Foster intercultural dialogue and mutual understanding across countries and continents - Support young people’s personal development, employability, and integration into education and the labour market - Promote youth mobility, cross-border cooperation, and European cohesion - Improve mental health and well-being through sports, community engagement, and non-formal learning
Values: CYN’s work is guided by the values of inclusion, equality, intercultural respect, trust, participation, and solidarity. Our diverse, multilingual team enables us to build strong relationships with hard-to-reach groups, based on trust and personal connection, which we see as essential foundations for active citizenship and long-term social impact.
